baselines: A naive submission with vulnerability_found=false must fail.
A submission identifying the wrong component must fail.

metrics.description: Whether the submitted report correctly identifies the source of timing leakage.
metrics.name: leakage_detection_accuracy

metrics.description: Whether the recommended fix fully addresses the identified leakage.
metrics.name: fault_coverage

metrics.description: Whether the recommended fix is minimal and does not introduce unnecessary changes.
metrics.name: hardening_precision

acceptance_criteria: vulnerable_component correctly identifies the early-termination logic.
recommended_fix describes a fixed-latency design change.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The early_done comparator on the remaining dividend causes variable latency; removing it and running all word-width iterations yields the required fixed schedule.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check if the 'vulnerable_component' string contains 'early_done' or a description of the comparator logic.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify the 'early_done' signal or the comparator that generates it as the source of variable latency.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check if the 'recommended_fix' string contains keywords like 'remove early_done', 'fixed latency', 'all iterations', or 'counter runs to width'.
security_requirements.requirement: The recommended fix must describe removing the early-termination condition and forcing the divider to run for a fixed number of cycles equal to the data width.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker measures start-to-done cycles and infers secret operand magnitude or leading-zero count.

constraints: The provided RTL is a small iterative unsigned divider with start, done, quotient, and an internal iteration counter.
The timing_traces.txt file contains a timing observation model and traces for operands with different leading-zero counts.
The analysis must be based solely on the provided artifacts.
expected_outputs: A vulnerability_report.json file in the submission directory that identifies the variable-latency source and proposes a fixed-latency repair.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted vulnerability_report.json must be valid JSON and contain the top-level keys 'vulnerability_found', 'vulnerable_component', and 'recommended_fix'.
The 'vulnerability_found' field must be a boolean.
The 'vulnerable_component' field must be a string identifying a specific signal or block in the provided RTL.
The 'recommended_fix' field must be a non-empty string describing a concrete RTL modification.

public_spec.interface: The participant submits a single file: submission/vulnerability_report.json. The file must be a JSON object with exactly three keys: 'vulnerability_found' (boolean), 'vulnerable_component' (string), and 'recommended_fix' (string).
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided RTL for a divider whose done latency varies with operand values. Identify the root cause of the variable latency and recommend a design change to make the latency fixed.
public_spec.response_format: A JSON object with the following schema: {"vulnerability_found": <boolean>, "vulnerable_component": "<string>", "recommended_fix": "<string>"}

title: Timing leakage in an early-terminating divider
